Start with the distinction

The agent decides what to build, how to triage, and whether the work is good.

The CLI performs and checks the mechanics: discover a request, claim it, validate a manifest, write exact files, run a gate, commit or recover.

01

One executable, many command families

You invoke one binary. Its entry point assembles 16 command families; shared packages supply parsing, models, filesystem guards and result types.

Where it fits

Markdown skill actions describe the agent’s workflow. Their shell launchers call this CLI for deterministic operations. The CLI reads project state from files and Git, then returns text or JSON that the caller can act on.

It is a local command-line program. It is not the Kanban web application: queue-kanban is a separate Go module. Some commands do launch child processes or make HTTP requests; there is no application database in this module.

Vocabulary: a UR records a user request; a REQ is a work item derived from it. A manifest describes intended operations in structured data. A gate is a check required before the workflow can proceed.

main.go · mainarchive_fetch.go · FetchArchive

The recurring shape

command arguments
    → parse and bind an exact target
    → observe files / Git / prior evidence
    → make a plan or a phase decision
    → apply guarded mechanics when authorized
    → return CommandResult

A reading pattern, not a universal call stack. Simple helpers may return directly; mutating families add transactions and recovery.

Follow one command from input to output

A safe example is reading the status of an existing archived request. This command was run successfully using a binary built from the frozen source snapshot.

Example 1 · read a field

From this repository’s root, using its launcher:

skills/do-work/tools/do-work-cli.sh --format text \
  frontmatter get \
  do-work/archive/UR-098/REQ-505-move-selection-and-claim-behind-advance.md \
  status

# Observed stdout:
completed

The receipt used the snapshot-built binary with the same command arguments. It read the existing request and made no request changes.

1. main.go registers frontmatter

corehelpers.Handlers() maps the verb to handleFrontmatter.

2. CommandRuntime.Run parses the prefix

--format text is global; everything after frontmatter is passed to the handler. Global flags must precede the command.

3. The handler parses the document

requestmodel.ParseDocument reads frontmatter. The helper selects the named field and supplies exact text output.

4. The result renderer writes stdout

Text mode preserves the helper’s compatibility output. JSON mode uses the shared result schema; it is not simply the same text wrapped in JSON.

04

How a request moves through the tool

The important distinction is between choosing work, advancing the workflow and changing a request’s lifecycle state.

CommandQuestion it answersWhat to understand
nextWhich queue requests are eligible?Resolves selectors, dependencies, priority, depth and fan-out. Does not claim. Blocked-check probes can run, so “read-only selection” does not mean “executes no processes.”
advanceWhat is the next valid step?Queue mode composes selection and claim. Working mode inspects fields/sections, returns a judgment phase or runs supplied mechanical gates.
claim / complete / fail / cancelHow should this exact request change state?Lower-level requeststate transitions with coupled checkpoint, archive and metadata plans.
finalizeHow do we finish this request and its Git record?Uses an authored manifest and a persisted journal to compose state changes, optional release and exact commits.
recoverWhat interrupted work needs reconciliation?Runs finalization recovery first, then applies claim-recovery rules. It is an active workflow operation.
recover-finalizationWhere did completion stop?Resumes journals or discovers a provable legacy tail; ambiguous shared changes produce a refusal.
next_selection.go · Selectqueue_commands.go · handleQueueAdvancerecovery_commands.go · handleRecover

An illustrative claimed request has a recognized route but no ## Triage section. The classifier returns “agent judgment: triage and open questions”. It does not invent a triage decision.

After required fields and sections exist, the next phase may be estimate-p50, preflight, qualify, a test gate, review, lessons or finalization. Route A omits some B/C steps.

The three representations of a request

Original document bytes

The author’s frontmatter, body, comments and formatting.

Typed record + normalized evidence

IDs, status, route, timestamps and aliases for decisions. Unknown or damaged input remains visible through warnings.

Repository snapshot + dependency graph

Exact paths, duplicate identities, checkpoint claims and relationships between requests.

05

Why the write path is longer than the read path

A lifecycle operation may touch a request, a checkpoint, an archive folder, calibration data, release metadata and Git history. Those changes need a bounded plan and a recoverable record.

Plan → apply → verify

requeststate.BuildPlan resolves the target and computes the intended changes. ApplyPlan uses the transaction layer to perform them. Publication follows a similar manifest-to-plan pattern.

gittransaction distinguishes dirty target paths from unrelated work. It records owned mutations and can restore before-images when an operation fails. atomicfile checks a target’s regular-file identity and digest before replacement.

This is why “just move the Markdown file” misses much of the implementation: the move must agree with checkpoint ownership, related records and the Git result.

state_plan.go · BuildPlanstate_apply.go · ApplyPlanatomic_file.go · ReplaceExisting

Example 3 · another writer changes a file

The operation reads and records a target’s bytes. Before replacement, it checks the file again. If the identity or content digest changed, it returns an error instead of treating the earlier read as current authority.

Rollback also checks ownership. It must not remove or overwrite an object another writer has substituted.

These are implemented guards with regression scenarios; they are not a claim that every possible filesystem race is impossible.

·

Finalization persists its progress

  1. prepared
  2. lifecycle_applied
  3. release_applied
  4. primary_committed
  5. metadata_committed
  6. verified
  7. cleanup_complete

The journal records the manifest, before/after file images, digests and commit identities. The release step is conditional. For ordinary completion, provenance may require a second commit after the primary commit hash exists.

If interrupted, recovery compares current state with recorded images and resumes only when it can establish what belongs to the operation. Failures before a primary commit can attempt rollback; later phases preserve and reconcile committed work.

finalization_types.go · Journalfinalization_apply.go · advanceJournal

Where temporary evidence lives

Finalization journals resolve through git --git-path do-work-finalization. Gate, lane and timing evidence use Git-private stores; timing uses per-run/per-request JSONL under the Git common directory.

Git resolves these locations because worktrees can have a .git file rather than a normal directory. Private evidence is distinct from the tracked request’s human-readable record.

09

A practical way to read and change it

Read a vertical slice before reading the largest files. Start at the command, follow its handler, then inspect the model and guard functions it actually calls.

A first reading session


  1. See how the executable is assembled.

  2. Understand argv, dispatch and rendering.

  3. Find handleFrontmatter and follow a small real command.

  4. See why typed fields coexist with original document bytes.

  5. Read selection without state mutation.

  6. Read the plan before the apply code.

  7. Finish with the persisted completion phases.

Example 4 · add one command

  1. Choose the owning command family and inspect its existing Handlers() map.
  2. Implement a handler with the shared CommandHandler signature. Keep observation, planning and mutation boundaries explicit.
  3. Register the name in that family. A new family also needs an import and registration loop in main.go.
  4. Return typed findings and actionable argument arrays. Use the existing transaction/ownership primitives for writes.
  5. Add focused tests for the real failure or behavior, then check that help and result rendering expose the command correctly.

A maintenance walkthrough, not a source change performed by this report.

Tests explain the intended boundaries

For example, the suite contains these named checks:

  • TestSetScalarChangesOnlyAuthorizedBytes
  • TestDirtyTargetIsRefusedButUnrelatedDirtIsAllowed
  • TestRecoverFinalizationResumesJournalAfterLifecycleInterruption
  • TestBlockedProbeTimeoutKillsDescendantGroup

Open their files in the explorer to read fixtures and assertions. A test name records intended coverage; it is not a fresh passing result.

Platform-specific code deserves a separate look

The inventory includes Unix, Windows and unsupported-platform variants even though only the host platform was built. Build tags decide which files Go compiles; reading a Windows file does not establish Windows runtime support for every command.

The ownedprocess non-Unix implementation reports unavailable group operations. Blocked probes have their own implementation and interruption contract, separate from the shared process-group package.


Verification lanes are also more than a test command string: their fingerprints bind source, tools, environment and freshness. Skipped execution is not reusable green evidence.
